Scheduling the Repeatable Job

slaScan.queue.js adds a repeatable job to Redis; server.js schedules it once, on API startup — never app.js.

// Figure 6.4: scheduling a repeatable job (src/jobs/slaScan.queue.js)
import { Queue } from 'bullmq';
import connection from '../config/redis.js';
import env from '../config/env.js';

export const QUEUE_NAME = 'sla-scan';

export const slaScanQueue = new Queue(QUEUE_NAME, { connection });

export const scheduleSlaScan = async () =>
  slaScanQueue.upsertJobScheduler(
    'sla-scan-repeatable',
    { every: env.SLA_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS },
    {
      name: 'scan',
      opts: {
        attempts: 3,
        backoff: { type: 'exponential', delay: 5_000 },
      },
    },
  );

A Job Scheduler is BullMQ's own object for "keep adding a job on this recurring pattern," identified by the id in the first argument ('sla-scan-repeatable') — creating one is what makes a job keep coming back on its own, every SLA_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS, without anything in this project calling .add() again. upsertJobScheduler — upsert, not create — matters because scheduleSlaScan() runs every time the API process starts (see below): calling it again with the same id updates that same schedule instead of creating a second one running alongside it, so restarting the API under npm run dev never leaves two scans running side by side. attempts/backoff are the retry behaviour flagged back in "Queues and Workers" — a scan that throws gets retried up to three times, waiting longer between each attempt.

// Figure 6.5: scheduling it from server.js, not app.js (src/server.js)
import { scheduleSlaScan } from './jobs/slaScan.queue.js';

const httpServer = http.createServer(app);
initSocket(httpServer);

scheduleSlaScan();

httpServer.listen(env.PORT, () => { /* ... */ });

Same reasoning as initSocket() right above it: this needs a real Redis connection, which a test importing app.js directly via supertest (CLAUDE.md's app.js/server.js split) should never be forced to have running. Calling scheduleSlaScan() only writes a repeat schedule to Redis — it doesn't run the scan itself. Actually running it is the worker's job, covered next.
